workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fix background tasks failing with sentry-sdk 3. Target files: pyproject.toml. New environments install `sentry-sdk` 3.0.0, released on 2026-11-23, and the server then fails: every pipeline and scheduled task raises `AttributeError: module 'sentry_sdk' has no attribute 'start_transaction'`, so runs, instances, fleets, gateways and volumes are not processed. With `DSTACK_SENTRY_DSN` set, `sentry_sdk.init` raises `TypeError: Unknown option 'enable_tracing'`. pyright fails in CI for the same calls. (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4514)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Verda backend cannot provision any instance (CPU or GPU): both hardcoded OS images were retired
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [Verda] Fix provisioning by switching to current OS images. Target files: src/dstack/_internal/core/backends/verda/compute.py, src/tests/_internal/core/backends/verda/test_compute.py. Verda instances failed to provision with `NO_OFFERS` because Verda removed the two OS images that `dstack` booted them from. (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4507)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: `exited (-1)` status when the job's process is killed by a signal
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Report signals in job exit status. Target files: runner/internal/runner/executor/executor.go, runner/internal/runner/executor/executor_test.go, src/dstack/_internal/core/models/runs.py. When a signal killed the job's process, the runner reported exit status -1, the value of os.ProcessState.ExitCode() for any signal, and the job was shown as `exited (-1)`. (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4490)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: `dstack apply -f` crashes when the configuration is outside the current directory
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fix dstack apply -f for configurations outside the current directory. Target files: src/dstack/_internal/cli/services/configurators/__init__.py, src/dstack/_internal/cli/services/configurators/base.py, src/tests/_internal/cli/services/configurators/test_configurators.py. . - Fix `dstack apply -f` and `dstack delete -f` crashing with `ValueError` for a configuration outside the current directory; its path is now kept absolute. - Document the `load_apply_configuration` argument and the returned configuration path. (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4471)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Kubernetes runs keep failing after the jump pod is evicted
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Kubernetes: manage the jump pod with a ReplicaSet. Target files: src/dstack/_internal/core/backends/kubernetes/compute.py, src/dstack/_internal/core/backends/kubernetes/resources.py, src/dstack/_internal/core/backends/kubernetes/utils.py. The jump pod was a bare pod, reused for as long as it existed. Once evicted, for example due to node pressure, it stayed in the Failed phase and was never recreated, so every job in the project failed until someone deleted the pod by hand. (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4447)
Fix: Fix unit tests with older `azure-mgmt-compute`. Applied modifications to pyproject.toml. (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4435)
Fix: Fix unit tests with older `openai`. Applied modifications to pyproject.toml. (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4437)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Kubernetes: job pod gets stuck in a restart loop
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Scope runner pull, metrics and stop to the job submission. Target files: runner/internal/runner/api/http.go, runner/internal/runner/api/server.go, runner/internal/runner/api/server_test.go. The server could not tell the runner it submitted a job to from another one at the same address. A container restarted by the backend (e.g., Kubernetes' default `restartPolicy: Always`) answers /api/pull with no job states, which the server took for a healthy running job, while the new runner waited for a submission that never came, exite... (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4425)
